exercise1.prompt: Labels and Honesty: The headline sentence

hiddenCases.name: the gap is measured, not assumed
the leader is whichever team is actually highest
the summary is computed, not typed
hiddenCases.describe: the means come from a group-by

exercise1.hint: Group to a mean per team, round to one place, then use idxmax and idxmin for the names. The gap is the difference between the two means.

exercise2.prompt: Labels and Honesty: How big is the gap, in context

hiddenCases.name: a large gap reads large both ways
the gap is between group means, not rows
the summary is computed, not typed
hiddenCases.describe: the means come from a group-by

exercise2.hint: Group to means, take max and min, subtract for the gap, then divide the gap by the minimum and multiply by 100. Round both at the end.

questions.prompt: A chart without units is what?
choices: Fine if the title is clear
questions.explain: The reader cannot tell pounds from thousands of pounds from a percentage.

questions.prompt: A bar chart whose y-axis starts at 80 rather than 0 does what?
choices: Exaggerates the differences between the bars
questions.explain: It can be defensible, but it is an argument and it has to be labelled as one.

questions.prompt: What belongs in a chart alongside the title and axis labels?
choices: How many observations it rests on
questions.explain: A difference between two rows and a difference between two thousand look identical on a chart.

questions.prompt: Reporting totals rather than rates is what kind of decision?
choices: One that can change which group looks best
questions.explain: Totals favour the big region and rates favour the small one, and the reader will not see you choose.
